prompt: A single pulley fixed to a beam above a well lets you pull down on a rope to lift a bucket. What does this fixed pulley actually do for you?

options.text: It halves the force needed to lift the bucket
It lifts the bucket twice as fast as you pull
It stores energy so the bucket rises on its own
It changes the direction of your pull, but not the size of the force needed

explanation: A single fixed pulley only changes the direction of the force — you pull down and the load goes up. The force needed is about the same as the load's weight.
